newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Christmas rally boosts Euro-bourses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Christmas rally boosts Euro-bourses.

text.p: European bourses extended their midday gains on Friday afternoon after Wall Street surged another one percent following its big two percent rally on Thursday.
London's FTSE 100 index opened at a record high while France's CAC 40 and Germany's DAX indices also latched onto Wall Street's coat tails.
"The Dow's jump overnight was unbelievable. It certainly has given the market a boost in confidence," one senior dealer in London said.
British and German government bonds both opened confidently, boosted by Thursday's strong bond rally in the United States.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar was little changed but analysts said the outlook remained bullish, with a raft of European economic data on Friday pointing to slow growth and benign price pressures across the continent.

The U.S. bond rally helped the Dow Jones industrial average soar 126.87 points to 6,473.64 overnight in its second biggest point gain ever. It surged another 60 points or so in the first ten minutes trading on Friday. The Dow's rise triggered program trading curbs.
"This may be the start of the Santa Claus rally," Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at U.S.-based Legg Mason Wood Walker said referring to Thursday's rally.
After recent jittery performances by stock markets, Wall Street's surge came as a morale boost for European bourses.

Britain's FTSE 100 index of leading shares opened 45.1 points higher at 4,096.4. But mild profit-taking and the expiration of FTSE index futures and options contracts nudged prices off their earlier all-time highs.
By 1500 GMT the FTSE was at 4,093.9, up 42.6 points or 1.05 percent.
When the FTSE's previous intraday trading high of 4,094.4, was reached on November 26, shares quickly retreated, ending the day at 4,068.4.
But another strong showing on Wall Street may be enough to keep the FTSE above its previous closing record of 4,073.1, dealers said.

"A new closing high is definitely within sight after the Dow rally," the head of sales and trading at a large brokerage said. "An assault on the 4,100 level is also possible today but we may fall a bit short."

German shares opened floor trading higher, boosted like bourses elsewhere by the Wall Street rally but also helped by a strong government bond market and the recent strength of the dollar. Prices later shaded lower.
"The firm dollar, Wall Street and Bunds are all responsible for taking us into the heavens," said one dealer.
The rally was spearheaded by the car sector including BMW AG, Volkswagen and Daimler-Benz, which saw the 30-share DAX index rise 1.6 percent to 2,854 by 1500 GMT.
In Paris, shares added one percent to the CAC index in opening trades, building on Wall Street's overnight run, and were up over 1.5 percent by mid-afternoon.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar was slightly softer against the mark and slightly firmer against the yen as traders wound down ahead of the holiday.

"If it is possible to discern a theme from today it's that there is still a strong chance of further repo cuts in Germany and, while all of Europe is tigthening fiscally, core European currencies should cheapen against the dollar," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5557 marks and 114.17 yen, compared with 1.5597 marks and 114.07 yen in late European business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 42.6 points, or 1.05 percent, at 4,093.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 35.42, or 1.58 percent, at 2,284.12.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 46.70 points, or 1.66 percent, at 2,854.45.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $369.00 compared with Thursday's close of $369.05.
